title: Buying his first bass and first job with Isaiah
summary: He bought a bass for $7 from Marrero with shoeshine money. Marrero pasted a paper keyboard on the fingerboard. His first job was a picnic gig with Isaiah.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Before we go into that boat and all, you remember the very first job you ever played and the first band you ever played?

Yeah. Yeah. Well, it was during the time I was learning. When I first started, I bought the bass about the day after Lent, right after Mardi Gras. Yeah. The Simon Mare. He sold me a bass for $7. I'll never forget. And I had been working as a shoeshine boy then out on Royal St. Charles Street and like that in those shoeshine things. And I made nice money. I had about $40 then. And I gave him money to buy me a bow and strings and paid him for the bass. So I never forget. He bought everything and strung the bass up.

Yeah, for the bass. Yeah. And I paid him for the rest of the stuff. He bought me strings and the bow and the rosin, everything I had to go with it. And he strung it up for me. He says, well, now right from here you're going to start your scales. And he got one of those bass methods. They have a keyboard on a fingerboard. Yeah. Yeah. So the piano has a keyboard, see. And so he cut that out as a piece of paper and pasted it on my fingerboard. Yeah. Yeah. And from there, we went from there. I started studying that thing. Yeah. Yeah. And he showed me the different keys. Like you see guys when you say, you really, that's, when you study that, those are the notes you're supposed to make the changes.
When you started, were you bowing mostly or picking?

Well, mostly bowing. Because he wanted me to start to, see, that's, that's the, you get the sound on the bass better, like that, see, when you're bowing. So, so I, I did pretty good during the Lent months and, and when the season did open up that Easter, first job I had was with my brother, Isaiah. Oh, yeah. He brought me up with his little band. Just, just that, that one job, you know. I, I played with him. He had a little gig, we call them nowadays. So, one of those picnics. Oh, yeah. On the, on the, on the, Millenburg, yeah. And I went with him. So, gee, I did pretty good. I used to go to rehearsals, you know, with different little groups and carol, just to get in practice like that, you know. But I couldn't play with the, the fast bands. And, but I find myself in the first tune I remember playing was the Sheik of Arab Eve. The first tune.
